title: PUAKILLER Rule Catalog
description: Source of truth for the PUA rule registry compiled into both removal scripts. Describes only the DECLARATIVE fields: Dirs and RegPaths are computed at runtime and written back into the hashtable by hosted-removal.ps1:1085-1087, so they are deliberately absent here.

bad_signers.description: Code-signing subjects abused almost exclusively by this cluster. A signer match drives Invoke-CertSweep, which deletes whole application roots, so entries must be distinctive shell-company subjects -- never a generically named vendor.

commentBlock.description: Verbatim PowerShell comment lines, re-emitted unchanged by the compiler. These carry the safety rationale for each entry and must survive regeneration.

id.description: Stable slug, independent of Name, so a rename does not orphan provenance.

Name.description: Exact install-folder name. Drives an UNCONDITIONAL folder sweep across LOCALAPPDATA, APPDATA, Programs, Start Menu, ProgramFiles(x86) and ProgramData. The most destructive field in the model: a short or generic Name deletes legitimate software. The minimum length is a structural guard, not a style rule -- short vendor folders belong in Aliases, where evidence is required first.

Label.description: Banner / verification display name. Empty string hides the entry, used for a second helper entry of the same product.

Rx.description: Case-insensitive regex matched against process paths, Run values, App Paths, COM classes, uninstall entries, tasks, shortcuts, droppers and Temp items. Stored VERBATIM and never regenerated by the compiler: most of these patterns encode hand-written false-positive reasoning.

Proc.description: Exact process names to kill, without .exe. Never a generic name (node, msiexec, chrome, setup, shift): generic executables are matched by path through Rx instead, which is what keeps legitimate apps alive.

Pub.description: Optional publisher regex for Add/Remove Programs entries, and one of the accepted evidence signals for a guarded alias. Empty string means no publisher is pinned.

Nw.description: Also clean NW.js (nw*) Temp directories whose manifest matches Rx.

Harden.description: AppData-relative folders sealed against reinstall under -Harden.

Aliases.description: Additional install-folder names. Unlike Name, an alias folder is removed ONLY when static evidence (matching filename, registered hash, or signer) is found inside it. That asymmetry is what makes short or generic vendor folders such as 'OB' and 'Shift' safe to cover.

RegNames.description: Exact vendor registry key names, removed only when file evidence or a distinctive primary-key hit is present.

Hashes.description: SHA-256 indicators, lowercase 64-hex, checked by STATIC hashing in guarded alias folders and top-level downloaded executables. Never executed. A malformed digest silently disables the alias guard, so the format is enforced rather than trusted.

requires_manual_regex.description: True when Rx does not reduce to a bare literal. Such patterns are human-authored and must never be machine-regenerated.

provenance.description: Public references cited by the entry's comment block. Mechanically extracted, not interpreted; structuring these per indicator is manual work tracked by needs_provenance_review.

rationale.description: Optional prose explaining a safety decision (why no Proc is listed, why no Pub is pinned).

allOf.description: An alias is only safe because something else proves the folder belongs to the PUA. With no Hashes, Proc or Pub there is nothing to check, and the guard degrades into an unconditional delete.
